service.description: The parameters every Purchasing report takes: its organization (every one of the user's when empty), the page, and output csv for the export.

The evaluations of the user's organizations' suppliers in scope: the latest of each supplier by default (view all for every one), by supplier, result (ScorecardResult) and a score below, newest first; each with its period, result, score (Insufficient data never shown as a zero), the eligible receipts, each measure with its numerator and denominator (price variance amounts withheld from a user who may not read supplier prices), the response it drew and the evaluation time. canEvaluate for a SUPPLIER_SCORECARD_EDIT holder.

One evaluation: its supplier, organization, period, policy row and due-date basis, result, score and response; its measures with numerator, denominator, eligible and excluded evidence, value, score, weight, range and criterion row; its evidence (a page, by measure) with each source, due date and basis, latest promise, event, quantity, counted share and why it was left out; the supplier's risks with the organization; and its other evaluations, newest first. Refuses an evaluation of another organization or a supplier outside the scope (RECORD_UNAVAILABLE).

Supplier360's Performance tab: the supplier's latest evaluation with the user's organizations, its measures and the supplier's active risks, and whether the user may evaluate or record a risk. Refuses a supplier outside the scope (RECORD_UNAVAILABLE).

Purchase spend over a period (90 days to now by default) by supplier, product or month (groupBy) and currency, in four measures never added together: committed (placed purchase order lines less cancelled, by placed date), received (receipts at the order's price), billed (supplier bills by bill date) and paid (payments applied by applied date; not by product), with totals per currency. Committed and received need a supplier-price reader (a buyer, approver, supplier-price or financial reader), billed also a payables reader, paid a finance reader; a measure the user may not read is withheld and named. Landed costs are Accounting's allocation. Refuses a period that ends before it starts or is over two years (PERIOD_INVALID).
Home's SpendSummary: committed and billed spend of the last three months by month and currency, as get#PurchaseSpend, with its snapshot time and what it withheld.

The budget commitments (Accounting's BudgetCommitment) of the organizations' purchase requests, purchase orders and bills, each stage once: a request reservation's open part (less what its order converted), the order's open part (less what its bill's actual converted) and the actual, so a reservation, its order and its actual count once; with totals per currency of reserved, ordered and actual. By supplier, stage, commitment date and view (open, the default, or all). Amounts need a financial reader (ACCOUNTING_VIEW or ACCOUNTING_ADMIN); others see the rows with their amounts withheld.

Each purchase request line through its requirement, RFQ, quotes and award to its purchase order lines, and each order line through its receipts (partly received named), inspections, bills, match and payment; a row per order line, so split suppliers, orders and bills stay apart. For a purchase request, a purchase order, or the period's requests and orders (90 days by default, by supplier). A bill's payment shows to a finance reader only, withheld (never unpaid) for anyone else. Refuses a request or order outside the scope (RECORD_UNAVAILABLE).

A product's buying history over a period (a year by default), by product, supplier and facility: the quotes' lines and each placed purchase order line, the quoted, ordered and billed unit prices kept apart in the document's currency and unit, with the lead time from placing to the first receipt. Prices need a supplier-price reader; others see them withheld.

A supplier's statement with the user's organizations over a period (90 days by default), per currency: the opening balance, each bill, credit and payment in date order with the running balance, and the closing balance; no bank details. For a finance reader only (ACCOUNTING_VIEW or PAYABLE_VIEW: PERMISSION_DENIED); refuses no supplier (SUPPLIER_REQUIRED) and one outside the scope (RECORD_UNAVAILABLE).
